findings.title: Make `unsubscribe_url` optional in the shared `unsubscribe_link` string
Stop mutating state on a non-idempotent GET request
Publish the notification-level change instead of saving the record directly
Align the confirmation text with the actual resulting state

response: ## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Title: Make `unsubscribe_url` optional in the shared `unsubscribe_link` string Affected: - config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855 - lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 Explanation: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` uses this string for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, in both the HTML part and, likely, the text body. This change only passes `unsubscribe_url` from the post-notification path in `UserNotifications`. Other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link` (digests, for example) do not pass it. For those emails, `I18n.t` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, so the email fails to send. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing, which points to the same problem. Use a separate translation key for the per-topic sentence and only append it when `unsubscribe_url` is present. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby # server.en.yml # unsubscribe_link: "To unsubscribe from these emails, visit your [user preferences](%{user_preferences_url})." # unsubscribe_link_and_topic: "...user prefs... To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})." key = @template_args[:unsubscribe_url].present? ? 'unsubscribe_link_and_topic' : 'unsubscribe_link' unsubscribe_link = PrettyText.cook(I18n.t(key, template_args)).html_safe ~~~ ## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Title: Handle a missing `TopicUser` record in `unsubscribe` Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-113 Explanation: `TopicUser.find_by` returns `nil` when the user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. This can happen, for example, when the user is notified through category watching or a mention without ever opening the topic. In that case `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError`, and clicking the email link returns a 500 error. Use `TopicUser.change`, or `find_or_initialize_by`, and treat a missing level as regular. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) current = tu.try(:notification_level) || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] new_level = current > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ? TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] : TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted] TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security Title: Stop mutating state on a non-idempotent GET request Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-116 - config/routes.rb:440-441 Explanation: The unsubscribe action changes notification state on a plain GET, and the change is not idempotent: - The first hit drops Watching/Tracking to Regular. - The second hit (page refresh, browser prefetch, or an email security scanner following links) drops Regular to Muted. There is also no CSRF protection. Any page can embed `` and silently mute topics for a logged-in victim. Fix options: - Make the GET only render a confirmation page, and do the change via POST/PUT with a CSRF token. - Or make the action idempotent by always setting one fixed target level. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby # routes: GET renders page, POST performs change get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#show_unsubscribe", constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/} post "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe", constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/} ~~~ ## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug Title: Publish the notification-level change instead of saving the record directly Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-113 Explanation: `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`. That method publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus and keeps the related bookkeeping consistent. As a result, other open tabs keep showing the old notification state. The unsubscribe page's notifications button may also be stale if it relies on that message. Use `TopicUser.change(...)` so the update flows through the existing path. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug Title: Align the confirmation text with the actual resulting state Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7 - config/locales/client.en.yml:985 Explanation: The page always says "You will stop receiving notifications for ". However, Tracking/Watching is only lowered to Regular, and Regular users still get notified for replies and mentions. The message is misleading in that case. Show text that matches the resulting notification level, or always set the level to Muted when the text promises that notifications stop. Proposed fix: ~~~js stopNotificiationsText: function() { const level = this.get("model.details.notification_level"); const key = level === 0 ? "stop_notifications" : "reduced_notifications"; return I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe." + key, { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") }); }.property("model.fancyTitle", "model.details.notification_level") ~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_users row for the topic, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level when clicking the email unsubscribe link
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when no record exists, and subsequently calling methods on the nil object (tu.notification_level or similar) will cause an error (NoMethodError/nil pointer exception). The golden comment mentions 'calling methods on it will crash' and the candidate specifically identifies 'NoMethodError on tu.notification_level'. They're describing the exact same bug.

false_positives.candidate: unsubscribe_link interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} but other mailers that set add_unsubscribe_link (like digests) do not pass it, causing I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and failing to send emails

Unsubscribe action changes notification state on a plain GET request which is not idempotent - first hit drops to Regular, second hit drops to Muted, and lacks CSRF protection allowing silent topic muting via embedded images
tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change which publishes notification_level_change on MessageBus, causing other open tabs to show stale notification state

Confirmation text always says 'You will stop receiving notifications' but Tracking/Watching only lowers to Regular where users still get notified for replies and mentions, making the message misleading

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
